Alexander's interest in Homer extended to fine details, and he even became involved in issues of textual editing. With all this drama about things like 'you guys are hypocrites because you complain about safe spaces but make your own' and whatnot has got me thinking. How about we have a system where each subverse that has, say, over 1000 subscribers, has to pick one of three categories to classify itself as: Neutral, Circlejerk, Culture.

I define these categories as the following:

Neutral - A subverse where views expressed are bipartisan spanning many points of view. This is where people go to discuss topics with people of opposing viewpoints, and the moderators' purpose is to be bipartisan and make sure the content follows Voat's rules, remove spam and keep general order, and the subverse owner's purpose is to keep the moderators in line.

Circlejerk - A subverse where views expressed are the same as the general userbase's. This is where people go to blow off steam, talk about common viewpoints and share resources to better improve personal knowledge about the views a user already has. The moderators' purpose is to make sure the content follows Voat's rules, remove spam, and remind people that it is a circlejerk. The subverse's owner's purpose is to keep the moderators in line.

Culture - A subverse for users with a common interest to discuss their hobby or whatever. The purpose of the moderator's is to make sure the content follows Voat's rules, remove spam and make sure the content is relevent, but are typically a lot more hands off than Neutral or Circlejerk mods.

I propose that each of these categories has a system where mods can impeach the owner to displace and replace them, so that the owners aren't invulnerable with potential to become tyrants. Also no circlejerk subverses can become default subverses.
